title: About Otter
text:
About Otter Otter is a programming language designed so that a program can be understood when it is read aloud. Otter was created by Jeffrey Macy. It is written in Windows PowerShell 5.1, and it runs on the PowerShell that is already part of Windows 10 and Windows 11. The idea Most languages ask you to learn punctuation before you can express an idea. Otter asks for the idea. Statements read as sentences, blocks end with a period, and each statement has exactly one meaning, so a beginner can read a program aloud and know what it does - and the computer can read it exactly one way. age is 20
if age is at least 18
    say "Adult"
. Otter Copy What Otter is today Otter is a pre-release, version {{RELEASE_VERSION}}. The language, the command-line tools, desktop and web application support, and the standard library are all in active use. Otter runs on Windows only for now. Design philosophy The reasoning behind the language - why properties use of, why a period only ever ends a block, why one canonical spelling beats many - is written down. Readable like English Structural words Period and block rules Philosophy License and credits Otter is free to use, including for commercial software. See the license page for exactly what you can and cannot do. The Otter Free Use License Third-party notices

title: The otter command
text:
The otter command One launcher runs programs, checks them, manages projects, and compiles web applications. Commands otter                          # start the interactive REPL
otter <file.ot>                # run a program (shortest form)
otter run <file.ot|project>    # run a program or project
otter check <file.ot|project>  # validate without running
otter test [target]            # run tests in a project or test file
otter build [target]           # build a project into dist/
otter publish [target]         # package a project into publish/
otter new <type> <name>        # create a project: console, desktop, web, automation, game
otter web <file.ot>            # compile to a web application and open it
otter desktop <file.ot>        # run a desktop app with the system bridge
otter studio                   # launch Otter Studio
otter help                     # show help
otter --version                # show the version PowerShell Copy Running programs otter run hello.ot and otter hello.ot do the same thing. Anything after the file name is passed to the program in its built-in arguments list: say "Arguments received:" length of arguments

each arg in arguments
    say "  Arg:" arg
. Otter Copy Running otter run script.ot deploy staging prints Arguments received: 2, then each argument on its own line. Checking without running otter check parses a program or a whole project and reports the first problems it finds. Nothing is executed and no files are touched, so it is safe on any file, and it suits editors and automated checks. Web applications otter web app.ot              # compile and open in your browser
otter web app.ot -NoOpen      # compile only; writes app.html next to the source PowerShell Copy Options -NoOpen         with otter web: write the HTML but do not open a browser
-Port <n>       with commands that host something: the port to use
-ParseOnly      check that a file is well formed and stop
-DebugTokens    print the tokens the lexer produced (for people working on Otter)
-DebugAst       print the syntax tree the parser produced
-DebugErrors    show the underlying PowerShell error instead of the friendly one Otter Copy Exit codes Scripts and automated checks can rely on these to tell why otter stopped: 0   success
1   usage error: unknown command, missing argument, file not found, wrong extension
2   the source does not parse (a syntax problem)
3   a well-formed program failed while running Output Copy Configuration Otter has no global configuration file. A project is configured by its otter.json manifest (see Projects). The one environment variable Otter reads is OTTER_BROWSER_USER_DATA_DIR, which chooses the browser profile folder used by otter desktop. If otter is not recognized, open a new terminal so it picks up the PATH, or run the launcher by its path. See Troubleshooting. Projects Troubleshooting

title: Working with collections
text:
Working with collections Measure, order, search, and pick items from lists. Collection Length The same readable syntax works with collections: say length of games Otter Copy Example: games are
    "Zelda"
    "Mario"
    "Pokemon"
.

say length of games Otter Copy Output: 3 Output Copy First and Last say first of games
say last of games Otter Copy Example: say first of games
say last of games Otter Copy If the collection is empty: say first of games Otter Copy returns: gone Output Copy The same applies to: say last of games Otter Copy Reverse Collections reverse games Otter Copy This reverses the current order of the collection. Find One Item Otter uses find when the programmer wants one matching item. find game in games where game is "Mario" into result Otter Copy The first matching item is placed into result. If nothing matches: result is gone Otter Copy This allows: find game in games where game is "Mario" into result

if result is gone
    say "Mario was not found."
otherwise
    say "Found" result
. Otter Copy Find With Object Properties find becomes especially useful with objects: find file in files where extension of file is ".pdf" into result Otter Copy Then: if result is gone
    say "No PDF found."
otherwise
    say "Found" name of result
. Otter Copy Derived Operations and Object Properties Not every expression using of represents a stored property. These are object properties: say name of file
say extension of file
say age of person Otter Copy These are operations: say length of games
say uppercase of name
say first of games Otter Copy They share readable surface grammar, but the parser may represent them differently internally. The runtime object model should not pretend every derived operation is a stored property.

title: Conditions
text:
Conditions if and otherwise choose what runs. Indentation defines the block; a period finishes it. There are no braces and no end keyword. age is 20

if age is at least 18
    say "Adult"
otherwise
    say "Minor"
. Otter Copy Adult Output Copy Comparison words is                 equal to
is not             not equal to
is greater than    greater than
is at least        greater than or equal to
is less than       less than
is at most         less than or equal to PowerShell Copy Chaining conditions Test several branches with otherwise if: score is 85

if score is at least 90
    say "Grade: A"
otherwise if score is at least 80
    say "Grade: B"
otherwise
    say "Grade: C"
. Otter Copy Grade: B Output Copy Truthiness A condition can also be a plain value. Text and lists are true when they are not empty, numbers are true when they are not zero, and gone is false. A variable that does not exist is an error - never silently false. Recovering from errors try runs a block; if something in it fails, the otherwise block runs instead of stopping the program. The period after a block is optional where indentation is already unambiguous, and it makes nested code explicit. It is never used for property access. Next: loops

title: CSV and downloads
text:
CSV and downloads Otter reads and writes RFC 4180 CSV natively. Each column header becomes a property of a row object. rawCsv is "id,city,temp 101,Seattle,68 102,Portland,72 103,Spokane,75"

convert rawCsv from csv into records

say "Loaded" length of records "weather records:"
each row in records
    say "  City:" city of row "High:" temp of row
. Otter Copy Loaded 3 weather records:
  City: Seattle High: 68
  City: Portland High: 72
  City: Spokane High: 75 Output Copy Reading and writing CSV files filePath is "weather.csv"

write csv records to filePath
read csv from filePath into loadedData
say "Verified" length of loadedData "rows read from disk."

delete file filePath Otter Copy Downloading files download streams a file from an HTTP or HTTPS address to a local path: url is "https://httpbin.org/robots.txt"
dest is "robots.txt"

download file from url to dest

if file dest exists
    read dest into text
    say "Downloaded" length of text "bytes."
    delete file dest
. Otter Copy Built-in download safety Otter never silently overwrites an existing file - the download stops before making any network request. Data streams into a hidden temporary file and is renamed into place only after every byte arrives. If the connection drops or the transfer is truncated, the partial file is removed. Next: networking

title: Databases
text:
Databases Describe a connection with has, connect to it, then run SQL with execute and query. Values are passed as named parameters, never pasted into the SQL text. Connecting database has
    provider is "sqlite"
    connection is ":memory:"
.

connect database into db Otter Copy A connection is a value like any other. disconnect db closes it. Using a connection after it is closed, or naming a table that does not exist, produces a readable Otter error. Changing data execute runs a statement that changes data. parameter "name" is value supplies @name in the SQL safely; into stores a result you can inspect. execute db with
    "create table if not exists tasks (id integer primary key autoincrement, title text, completed integer, priority text)"

execute db with
    "insert into tasks (title, completed, priority) values (@title, @completed, @priority)"
    parameter "title" is "Buy groceries"
    parameter "completed" is 0
    parameter "priority" is "high"
into insertResult

say "Rows affected:" rows affected of insertResult
say "New id:" last inserted id of insertResult Otter Copy A parameter can be gone, which is stored as a database NULL. Reading data query returns a list of row objects. Each column is a property of a row. query db with
    "select id, title, completed, priority from tasks"
into allTasks

each task in allTasks
    say title of task
    if priority of task is gone
        say "Priority: none"
    otherwise
        say priority of task
    .
. Otter Copy Looking at the schema get tables from db into tables

each table in tables
    say kind of table
    say name of table

    get columns from table in db into columns
    each column in columns
        say name of column
        say type of column
    .
. Otter Copy Databases are a console and desktop feature. The web target reports database statements as unsupported. Next: the query language

title: Dates and Time
text:
Dates and Time A date is a real Otter value, not text. today gives the current date; now gives the current date and time. date is today
started is now Otter Copy A date and a date-time are different today has no time of day at all â€” it is not midnight, it simply does not carry a time. now carries both a date and a time. This is a meaningful distinction, not a technicality: a date with "no time" and a date at "00:00:00" are not the same idea, so Otter does not pretend one is the other. Because of that, asking a plain date for its hour, minute, or second is invalid rather than answering with a silent zero: date is today
say hour of date Otter Copy That fails when it runs, with an error explaining that this date has no time of day. Reach for now when you need a time as well as a date. Reading the parts of a date Date parts are read the same way any other property is read â€” with of, not with a period. Year, month, and day work on both a date and a date-time: say year of date
say month of date
say day of date Otter Copy month of date is always a number from 1 to 12, never a month name. Hour, minute, and second work on a date-time such as started: say hour of started
say minute of started
say second of started Otter Copy Adjusting a date Move a date forward with add, or backward with remove. Both the singular and plural spelling of a unit are accepted, so 1 day and 7 days both work: add 7 days to date
remove 1 month from date Otter Copy The same words work on a date-time, down to the second: add 1 hour to started
add 30 minutes to started Otter Copy Formatting format ... as ... into ... produces text. It does not change the date it was given: format date as "MM/dd/yyyy" into text
say text
say date Otter Copy The second say still prints the original date, untouched. The difference between two dates days between is an expression, so assign it with the same is form used for every other value: startDate is date from "2024-01-15"
endDate is date from "2024-03-01"
waiting is days between startDate and endDate
say waiting Otter Copy The expression can also be used directly wherever a value is expected: startDate is date from "2024-01-15"
endDate is date from "2024-03-01"
say days between startDate and endDate Otter Copy The older days between ... make ... statement remains accepted for compatibility, but new programs should prefer the expression form. The result is signed, computed as end minus start: - positive â€” endDate is later than startDate - zero â€” the two are the same, at the precision asked for - negative â€” endDate is earlier than startDate Comparing dates Dates compare with the same words as any other value â€” there is no separate date-comparison syntax: startDate is date from "2024-01-15"
endDate is date from "2024-03-01"

if endDate is greater than startDate
    say "The end date is later."
. Otter Copy How a date prints say prints a date-only value like this: say today Otter Copy Example output: 2026-09-09 and a date-time value like this: say now Otter Copy Example output: 2026-09-09 14:30:05 Not part of this version There is no timezone syntax â€” a date is always in local time. There is no month-name syntax; month of date is always a number.

title: Readable like English. Precise like code.
text:
Readable like English. Precise like code. Otter favors language that can be read aloud without hiding program structure. age is 20

title: Diagnostic Output
text:
Diagnostic Output log, warn, and error send a message to Otter's diagnostic output rather than to the program's normal output. log "Server started."
warn "Connection is slow."
error "Could not connect." Otter Copy This page is about the log / warn / error statements. It is not about the messages Otter itself prints when a program has a syntax or runtime error â€” every reference page shows what those look like for the statement it covers. Diagnostics are not say say is what a program tells the person using it. log, warn, and error are what it tells whoever is running or operating it â€” a developer watching a console, a log file, a monitoring tool. Otter keeps the two separate on purpose: say "Welcome!"
log "Startup complete." Otter Copy A host running Otter can send say output to a user interface while sending diagnostics somewhere else entirely, such as a log file or a monitoring service, without the program needing to know or care. They travel on separate channels. Three levels All three take the same kind of message as say â€” one or more values, joined with a space: port is 8080
log "Listening on port" port Otter Copy log records something that happened normally. warn flags something that is not wrong yet but is worth attention. error reports something that failed. A realistic example port is 8080

say "Otter web server"

log "Starting up."
log "Listening on port" port
warn "No configuration file found, using defaults."
error "Could not reach the database."

say "Ready." Otter Copy Only the say lines are part of what the program is telling its user. The log, warn, and error lines went to the diagnostic channel.

title: Finding files and folders
text:
Finding files and folders Discover the files and folders inside a folder, with explicit control over whether subfolders are included. File Discovery Files can be discovered from a folder: get files in "Pictures" into files Otter Copy The result is a list of file objects. Example: get files in "Documents" into files

for each file in files
    say name of file
. Otter Copy Folder Discovery Folders can be discovered the same way: get folders in "Documents" into folders Otter Copy Example: for each folder in folders
    say name of folder
. Otter Copy Discovery Does Not Recurse By Default This: get files in "Pictures" into files Otter Copy only retrieves files directly inside Pictures. It does not automatically search subfolders. Recursive discovery must be requested explicitly: get files in "Pictures" and subfolders into files Otter Copy Likewise: get folders in "Documents" and subfolders into folders Otter Copy The phrase: and subfolders Output Copy is the only recursion switch for discovery.

title: File and folder objects
text:
File and folder objects A discovered file or folder is an object with properties you read with of. File Objects A discovered file is an object. Common file properties include: say name of file
say path of file
say extension of file
say size of file
say created of file
say modified of file Otter Copy Example: get files in "Pictures" into files

for each file in files
    say name of file
    say extension of file
    say size of file
. Otter Copy File operations may accept either a path or a file object. Path: move "photo.jpg" to "Pictures" Otter Copy Object: move file to "Pictures" Otter Copy Folder Objects A discovered folder is also an object. Folder properties include: say name of folder
say path of folder
say created of folder
say modified of folder Otter Copy A folder does not expose: say size of folder Otter Copy as a normal property. Determining the total size of a folder may require recursively examining many files and subfolders. Otter should not hide an expensive operation behind a property that appears inexpensive.

title: Files and Folders
text: Files and Folders Otter can work with text files and discover files or folders. File operations use explicit verbs. write \"Hello\" to \"note.txt\"\nread \"note.txt\" into note\nget files in \"Pictures\" into files Otter Copy

title: Files and folders
text:
Files and folders Otter has native, sandboxed file operations written as plain statements. notePath is "status.txt"

# Writing text to a file
write "Otter system: online and verified." to notePath

# Checking file existence
if file notePath exists
    say "Note file exists on disk."
.

# Reading file contents
read notePath into content
say "File content:" content

# Copying and deleting files
backupPath is "status-backup.txt"
copy notePath to backupPath

delete file notePath
delete file backupPath
say "Temporary files cleaned up." Otter Copy Note file exists on disk.
File content: Otter system: online and verified.
Temporary files cleaned up. Output Copy Watching files change A program can react to the file system as it happens. The watcher is real operating-system events, not polling: watch file "settings.json" and call it settingsWatcher

on change of settingsWatcher
    say "settings changed"
    stop watching settingsWatcher
. Otter Copy watch folder "reports" recursively and call it w also reports on change of, on create in, on delete in, and on rename in events with the path that changed. File watching is for console programs; the web target reports it as unsupported. Next: CSV and downloads

title: gone: the absence of a value
text:
gone: the absence of a value gone means no value exists. It is not the same as empty text, zero, an empty list, or false. Gone â€” Absence of a Value Otter uses: gone Output Copy to represent the absence of a value. gone is Otter's equivalent of concepts such as null, nil, or None in other programming languages. Example: user is gone Otter Copy Check for an absent value: if user is gone
    say "User was not found."
. Otter Copy Check that a value exists: if user is not gone
    say "Welcome" name of user
. Otter Copy gone is a literal value. It does not require special assignment syntax. user is gone Otter Copy uses the same assignment rules as: user is "Jeff" Otter Copy Gone Is Different From Empty and False These values are not equivalent: user is gone
name is ""
score is 0
games are empty
ready is false Otter Copy They mean: gone       no value exists
""         a string exists but contains no characters
0          a number exists and is zero
empty      a collection exists but contains no items
false      a boolean exists and is false Output Copy Otter must not automatically treat these values as interchangeable. Gone Is the Only Absence Keyword Otter uses only: gone Output Copy for absence. Do not introduce aliases such as: null
nil
None
nothing
NA Output Copy This keeps the language consistent and prevents multiple words from representing the same concept.

HTTP requests

HTTP requests get, post, put and delete talk to web services. They work the same in console programs and in web applications. Fetching get "https://api.example.com/data" into result
get "https://api.example.com/data" as json into data Otter Copy as json parses the body into ordinary Otter objects and lists that you read with of. Sending post "hello" to "https://api.example.com/echo" into reply
put "updated" to "https://api.example.com/items/1" into reply
delete from "https://api.example.com/items/1" into reply Otter Copy Options An indented block adds headers, cookies, redirect handling and a timeout to one request: get "https://api.example.com/data" into result

    with cookies
    following redirects
    with timeout 10 seconds Otter Copy A request that cannot complete, or that times out, is a readable Otter error you can handle with try and otherwise. Next: web servers

title: Installation
text:
Installation Otter needs Windows PowerShell 5.1 and nothing else. There are no administrator rights, services, or registry changes. Release status: {{RELEASE_CHANNEL}} {{RELEASE_VERSION}}. Windows installer: {{INSTALLER_STATUS}}. Until an installer is published, run Otter from the project folder (below). System requirements Windows 10 or Windows 11 (64-bit) with Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe, built into Windows). A standard user account is enough. A web browser is only needed for web applications. Otter runs on Windows PowerShell 5.1; the otter.cmd launcher finds it for you, so you can start Otter from Command Prompt, Windows Terminal, or PowerShell 7 alike. Run from the project folder Get the Otter project folder from GitHub, open Windows PowerShell in it, and run a program with otter.cmd: git clone https://github.com/Heavens-Lava/otterPS.git
cd otterPS
.\otter.cmd --version
.\otter.cmd examples\hello.ot PowerShell Copy No registry changes, environment variables, or background services are created. Add the folder to your PATH if you would like to type otter instead of .\otter.cmd. Install from a release archive When a versioned archive is published, extract it, open Windows PowerShell in the extracted folder, and run the per-user installer. It copies Otter to %LOCALAPPDATA%\Otter, adds it to your user PATH, and runs a health check: Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass
.\Install-Otter.ps1 -AddToUserPath PowerShell Copy Open a new terminal so the updated PATH takes effect, then verify: otter --version PowerShell Copy Otter {{RELEASE_VERSION}} Output Copy Verify your installation otter                  # starts the interactive REPL (type exit to leave)

title: Networking
text:
Networking WebSockets, TCP, UDP and TLS are ordinary Otter statements. Connections are named values, and things that happen to them are events you handle with on. Availability: this feature is in the current source tree and is not part of a published release yet. WebSockets A WebSocket delivers whole messages. It works in console programs and in web applications. connect to websocket "wss://echo.example.com" and call it chat

on open of chat
    send "Hello" through chat
.

on message from chat
    say "Got:" received message
    close websocket chat
.

on error of chat
    say "Problem:" websocket error
. Otter Copy chat is connecting, open, closing, or closed - check it with chat is open, or read state of chat. TCP TCP is a stream of bytes, not messages, so its event is on data from and what arrives is always bytes. Otter never converts between text and bytes silently: turn text into bytes yourself before sending it. connect to tcp "localhost" on port 9000 and call it connection

on connect of connection
    message is bytes from text "Hello from Otter"
    send message through connection
.

on data from connection
    data is received data
    say text from bytes data
    close tcp connection
.

on error of connection
    say network error
.

on close of connection
    say "Disconnected"
. Otter Copy Ask a connection about itself with state of connection (connecting, connected, closed), remote address of connection and remote port of connection. A connection that cannot be made goes to on error, then on close - or, with no on error handler, stops the program with a readable message. TCP servers (listen for tcp) are reserved grammar and are not available yet. TCP clients are. TLS Add securely to make the same connection over TLS. The system checks the certificate chain, expiry, revocation, and that the certificate matches the server name. There is no way to turn that off: an untrusted certificate simply fails the connection. connect securely to tcp "example.com" on port 443 and call it connection

on connect of connection
    if connection is secure
        say "secure"
    .
    say tls version of connection
. Otter Copy for server "name" checks the certificate against a different name than the address you connect to. On this runtime (Windows PowerShell 5.1) protocol negotiation is not available, so using protocol stops with a clear message rather than connecting without it. UDP UDP sends independent datagrams. Open a socket, listen for data, and send to an address and port. open udp on port 9000 and call it socket

on data from socket
    say "Received from" sender address
    response is bytes from text "Hello"
    send response through socket
        to sender address
        on port sender port
. Otter Copy open udp and call it socket picks a free port for you. close udp socket closes it. Where these run TCP, UDP and TLS are for console and desktop programs. A browser cannot open raw sockets, so the web target reports them as unsupported instead of imitating them. WebSockets work on both. Next: cryptography and secrets

PASS tests/app_test.ot

1 passed Output Copy Writing a test A test is an ordinary Otter file. It passes when it finishes and fails when it calls fail with: score is 100

title: The query language
text:
The query language For everyday reading of data you do not need to write SQL. get, where, order by and the aggregate words read like the question you are asking. Availability: this feature is in the current source tree and is not part of a published release yet. Getting rows get all from items in db into allItems
say "Count:" length of allItems

get name and price from items in db with

into sortedItems Otter Copy Filtering with where Conditions use the same words as if: is, is not, is at least, is less than, and, or, not, contains, is in, is between, and is gone for missing values. Values are always passed to the database as parameters, so text from a user cannot change the meaning of the query. minAge is 18
get all from users in db with

term is "Apple"

text:
State and reactivity Keep values that change in state, describe what is derived from them, and react when they change. state count is 0
derive doubled is count * 2

title: Reference
text:
Otter language reference An index of what Otter supports. Unsupported or experimental syntax is intentionally left out. Values and variables Text, numbers, booleans, lists, objects, bytes, and gone. Assignment with is; arithmetic with and, minus, times, divided by and make; add and remove. Read values and variables Conditions, loops, and functions if, otherwise, while, repeat, count, each, to, return, and stop. Comparison words: is, is not, is greater than, is at least, is less than, is at most. Read conditions Read loops Read functions Lists, objects, files, and folders Lists and collections, property access with of, objects with has, JSON, CSV, file discovery, and explicit file and folder operations. Read lists Read objects and properties Read files and folders Read CSV and downloads Networking, cryptography, and secrets WebSockets, TCP, UDP and TLS; hashing, signing, authenticated encryption and password hashing; and the operating-system credential vault. Read networking Read cryptography and secrets Desktop UI, events, and layout Create windows and controls, configure them with has, put resources into windows and row or column containers, handle events with when, and show a window: create button into saveButton
when saveButton is clicked
    say "Saved"
. Otter Copy State, derived values, and watchers Otter supports state, derive, and when a state value changes. Derivations update from their dependencies, and watchers run only when a value actually changes. Web applications otter web compiles a program into a standalone HTML, CSS, and JavaScript application. Pages, rows, columns, cards, links, buttons, text, images and more are declared with is a, and drag and drop is available with draggable and accepts drops. Errors and diagnostics Use try and otherwise for recoverable work. Otter also provides log, warn, and error for diagnostic output. Every error is a readable Otter message that names the line - never a raw stack trace. Read conditions and errors

title: Scope
text:
Scope Where a variable can be seen: everywhere, inside one function, or inside one block. Variable Scope Otter must define where variables can be accessed. Example: name is "Jeff"

to greet
    message is "Hello"
    say name
. Otter Copy The language must specify: - whether functions can read variables outside themselves - whether local variables disappear when the function ends - whether nested blocks create new scopes - how outer variables are changed deliberately The preferred rule is: Variables created inside a function belong to that function unless explicitly exposed. Function Local Variables Example: to greet name
    message is "Hello"
    say message name
. Otter Copy message exists only while greet is running. After the function finishes, message should no longer be available outside that function. Block Scope Simple control-flow blocks should not automatically hide ordinary variables unless Otter later chooses strict lexical block scope. Example: ready is true
if ready
    message is "Starting"
.

say message Otter Copy This behavior needs one consistent rule across: if
while
for each
count
try Output Copy The exact rule should be frozen before more advanced closures or concurrency are added.

title: Cryptography and secrets
text:
Cryptography and secrets Safe algorithms and parameters are the runtime's job. You say what you want - encrypt, hash a password, generate random bytes - not which cipher to use. Availability: this feature is in the current source tree and is not part of a published release yet. Bytes Everything here works on bytes, Otter's binary type. Text and bytes are never converted silently; ask for the conversion you mean: data is bytes from text "Hello"
say hex from bytes data
say base64 from bytes data
say text from bytes data
say length of data Otter Copy Hashing and signing data is bytes from text "abc"

digest is sha256 of data
say hex from bytes digest

key is bytes from text "shared secret"
signature is hmac sha256 of data using key
say hex from bytes signature Otter Copy sha256, sha384 and sha512 are available, and the same three for hmac. Obsolete hashes such as MD5 and SHA-1 are deliberately left out. Secure random bytes token is secure random bytes 32
say hex from bytes token Otter Copy This uses the operating system's cryptographically secure source, unlike Otter's general random numbers. Encryption Encryption is authenticated: tampered or wrongly-keyed data is refused, never returned as garbage. The nonce is handled for you and stored inside the result. generate encryption key and call it key

message is bytes from text "Attack at dawn"
encrypt message using key and call it encrypted
decrypt encrypted using key and call it original

say text from bytes original Otter Copy Attack at dawn Output Copy Store or send the result with base64 from bytes encrypted, and restore it with bytes from base64 encoded. Passwords Passwords are not hashed like other data. hash password uses a slow, salted algorithm chosen by the runtime and gives you text you can store safely: password is "correct horse battery staple"
hash password password and call it storedHash

if password password matches hash storedHash
    say "Correct"
. Otter Copy Comparing secrets securely equals compares bytes in constant time, so timing does not leak how much of a secret matched: if expected securely equals actual
    say "Valid"
. Otter Copy The credential vault Store secrets such as API tokens in the operating system's credential store instead of a file. Secrets are scoped to your program: two different Otter programs storing "api-token" never see each other's value. if secret "api-token" exists
    token is secret "api-token"
otherwise
    ask secretly "API token:" and call it token
    store secret "api-token" with value token
.

delete secret "api-token" Otter Copy A secret holds text or bytes and comes back as the same kind. Reading a secret that does not exist is an error, never an empty string. On Windows the vault is the Windows Credential Manager. Cryptography and the vault are console features. The web target reports them as unsupported - browser storage is not a secure credential store. Back to the reference

title: Build a Task Manager
text:
Build a Task Manager Build a small Windows task manager that accepts a task, adds it to a live list, and clears the box for the next one. What you will learn You will create a window, lay out rows and a column, configure a text box and button, handle a click, and create a new text control at runtime. Before you start You need Otter on Windows and a folder where you can save a .ot file. This is a native Windows application, so run it with otter tasks.ot rather than the browser Run button. Verify your installation 1. Create the window and the input area Start a new file named tasks.ot. A window holds the whole application. The header and input rows keep related controls together. The empty column below them becomes the live task list. create window into app
app has title "Otter Tasks"
app has width 420
app has height 520
padding of app is 20
spacing of app is 12

create row into header
header has width full
create text into titleText
titleText has text "My Tasks"
put titleText in header
put header in app

create row into inputRow
inputRow has width full
inputRow has spacing 8

create text box into taskInput
placeholder of taskInput is "What needs to be done?"
taskInput has width 280

create button into addButton
addButton has text "Add"

put taskInput in inputRow
put addButton in inputRow
put inputRow in app

create column into taskList
taskList has width full
taskList has spacing 8
put taskList in app Otter Copy 2. Add a task when the button is clicked The event reads the text box. It ignores an empty submission. For a real task, it creates a text control, places it in the list, and clears the input ready for another task. when addButton clicked
    task is text of taskInput
    if task is not ""
        create text into item
        item has text task
        put item in taskList
        text of taskInput is ""
    .
. Otter Copy 3. Show the window Finish with show app. Save the file, open PowerShell in that folder, and run otter tasks.ot. Type a task and select Add; a new line should appear in the list. show app Otter Copy Common problems If Otter cannot find tasks.ot, use cd to move PowerShell into the folder containing the file. If no task appears, make sure the event starts with when addButton clicked and the two periods close the if block and the event. Try next Add a second heading, change the button text, or give each new task a prefix such as - . Once that feels comfortable, try a counter or another input example. title: Troubleshooting
text:
Troubleshooting Most problems fall into a few groups. Otter error messages name the line, say what went wrong in plain words, and often suggest a fix - start by reading them. Installation and PATH "Running scripts is disabled on this system": allow scripts for the current terminal only. It expires when you close the window. Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process Bypass PowerShell Copy "otter is not recognized as an internal or external command": the terminal was opened before Otter was added to your PATH. Close it and open a new one. To check the PATH, run: [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path', 'User') PowerShell Copy You can always run Otter by its full path, for example & "C:\Tools\Otter\otter.cmd" hello.ot. Syntax errors A syntax error means Otter could not read the program. It shows the line, a marker where the problem is, and a suggestion. These are the real messages: Otter Syntax Error

Line 1:
    say "Hello
        ^

This string never closes.

Try:
    Add a closing quote. Output Copy Fix: close the text with a second double quote. Runtime errors A runtime error means the program is well formed but something went wrong while it ran. Otter Runtime Error

Line 1:
    say greeting

Otter could not find the variable "greeting". It has not been given a value yet.

Try:
    greeting is 0 Output Copy Fix: give the variable a value before you use it. Otter never guesses that a missing variable means empty or false. Otter Runtime Error

Line 1:
    say 10 divided by 0

I cannot divide by zero. Output Copy Fix: check the divisor first, with an if, before dividing. Otter Runtime Error

Line 4:
    greet

"greet" needs 1 value but was given 0.

Try:
    greet person Output Copy Fix: pass every value the function asks for. Otter Runtime Error

Line 2:
    add 1 to score

I can only add to a number or a list, but "score" holds some text. Output Copy Fix: make sure the variable holds a number: score is 0, not score is "high". File errors Otter Runtime Error

Line 1:
    read "missing.txt" into content

I could not find a file called "missing.txt".

Try:
    if file "missing.txt" exists Output Copy Fix: check the name and folder, or test for the file first. Relative paths are relative to the folder you ran otter from. if file "missing.txt" exists
    read "missing.txt" into content
    say content
otherwise
    say "There is no missing.txt yet."
. Otter Copy Common mistakes - A property is written property of thing (name of person), never person.name. - A block ends with a period on its own line. A period is never used for anything else. - Some words Otter uses in statements, such as percent, cannot be variable names. Pick another (rate instead of percent). - One calculation per statement: bill times rate make product, then product divided by 100 make tip. Reporting a problem If Otter reports "a bug in Otter", or a message is unclear, please open an issue with the smallest program that shows it, the exact message, your Otter version (otter --version), and your Windows version. Open an issue on GitHub The otter command

title: try and otherwise
text:
try and otherwise try runs a block; if something in it fails, otherwise handles it. Try and Otherwise Otter uses: try
    ...
otherwise
    ...
. Output Copy for error handling. Example: try
    read "settings.json" into settings
otherwise
    say "Could not load settings."
. Otter Copy If the try body completes normally, the otherwise body does not run. If an operation in the try body fails, Otter runs the otherwise body. Otherwise Is Optional for Try A try block may exist without an otherwise body when the runtime or surrounding code handles the failure. try
    read "settings.json" into settings
. Otter Copy The exact propagation behavior should follow Otter's runtime error rules. Normal Control Flow Is Not Failure Statements such as: return Output Copy must pass through try normally. Example: to find user
    try
        return user
    otherwise
        say "Could not find user."
    .
. Otter Copy If return user executes successfully, the function returns user. The otherwise body must not run. Normal control-flow changes are not runtime errors. This rule should also apply to future control-flow features such as: break
continue Output Copy

title: Values and variables
text:
Values and variables Otter works with text, numbers, booleans, lists, objects, and gone. Use is to give a value a name. name is "Alice"
age is 29
ratio is 3.14
active is true
missing is gone Otter Copy Variable names start with a lowercase letter and use camelCase (totalRevenue, userEmail). Names are case-sensitive. Text uses double quotes. Types are determined automatically. Saying values say prints its values on one line, separated by single spaces. Numbers print without trailing zeros and booleans as true or false. name is "Jeff"
age is 29
say name "is" age "years old." Otter Copy Jeff is 29 years old. Output Copy Arithmetic Calculations use everyday words. make stores the result: number1 is 10
number2 is 5

number1 and number2 make total
number1 minus number2 make difference
number1 times number2 make product
number1 divided by number2 make quotient

say "Total:" total
say "Difference:" difference
say "Product:" product
say "Quotient:" quotient Otter Copy Total: 15
Difference: 5
Product: 50
Quotient: 2 Output Copy Dividing by zero is a readable Otter error, never a crash. Changing a number in place score is 100

add 15 to score
remove 30 from score

say "Final score:" score Otter Copy Final score: 85 Output Copy Input ask converts what was typed: 42 becomes the number 42, true becomes a boolean, and everything else stays text. ask "Enter your age: " and call it age
age and 5 make futureAge
say "In 5 years you will be:" futureAge Otter Copy Using a variable that was never defined is an error, not false and not empty. Otter tells you which name it could not find. Next: conditions Comments A # starts a comment that runs to the end of the line. Comments are for people; Otter ignores them. A # inside quotes is just text. # This whole line is a comment.
age is 29   # so is the end of this line
say "#1 is not a comment"
say age Otter Copy Good comments explain why, not what: the code already says what.

Web applications otter web compiles an Otter program into a standalone HTML, CSS and JavaScript application. You write the page in Otter: no HTML, no build tool. otter web app.ot PowerShell Copy Describing a page Each part of the page is a named resource. is a declares it, with lets you set properties on the same line, and put places it inside another. app is a page with title "Greeter", width 560, background "#0f172a", spacing 14

Layout words such as spread, align middle and spacing arrange rows and columns. customstyle passes raw CSS for anything else. scroll true on a page lets it scroll like an ordinary website. go back Otter Copy Drag and drop Make things draggable, mark where they can be dropped, and react: card is panel with draggable is true

title: Introduction
text:
Welcome to Otter Otter is a readable programming language for useful programs, from small scripts to interactive web applications. Readable like English. Precise like code. Otter programs use everyday words and indentation instead of punctuation-heavy syntax, without giving up deterministic programming-language behavior. name is "World"
say "Hello" name Otter Copy Hello World Output Copy Programs you can read aloud Words express meaning directly: and, minus, times, divided by, is at least, is greater than. Blocks are finished with a period. Properties are read with everyday prepositions, such as name of developer. age is 20
if age is at least 18
    say "Adult"
. Otter Copy The period has exactly one structural meaning in Otter: it finishes a block or process. It is never used for property access. What Otter does today Variables and readable arithmetic, conditions and loops, lists, functions, objects, sandboxed file operations, CSV and JSON, command-line arguments, safe web downloads, a query language for databases, TCP/UDP/TLS networking, cryptography, and compilation of programs into standalone web applications. Otter runs on 64-bit Windows 10 and Windows 11 using Windows PowerShell 5.1, which is already installed. There is nothing else to set up. Where to go next Install Otter Write your first program Learn the language: values and variables

title: What can you build?
text: What can you build? Otter programs range from a one-line script to a full application. This is what the language supports today. Console programs and automation Ask for input, calculate, read and write files and folders, run other programs, and react when files change. Files and folders Command line Desktop applications Create a window, add controls, and react to events. The same program shows a native Windows interface. Windows applications Web applications otter web compiles a program into a standalone web page - pages, routes, forms, drag and drop - with nothing else to install or host. Web applications Web services and APIs Declare a web server, add routes, and respond with text or JSON. Call other services with get, post, put and delete. Web servers HTTP requests Data Read and write CSV, JSON and XML; talk to a database and ask questions of it in plain words. CSV and downloads Databases The query language Networking and security WebSockets, TCP, UDP and TLS connections; hashing, authenticated encryption, password hashing, and a credential vault for secrets. Networking Cryptography and secrets Bigger projects otter new creates a project with tests, and otter build and otter publish turn it into something you can hand to someone else. Projects

title: What is Otter?
text:
What is Otter? Otter is a programming language you can read aloud. Programs use everyday words and indentation instead of punctuation-heavy syntax, and they still behave exactly and predictably. name is "Otter"
say "Hello, " + name

to greet person
    say "Welcome, " + person
.

greet "Ada" Otter Copy Hello, Otter
Welcome, Ada Output Copy Readable like English. Precise like code. Every statement has one clear meaning. Words such as is, and, minus, is at least and of do the work that symbols do in other languages, so a program reads like a description of what it does. Blocks are closed with a period, and a period is never used for anything else. What runs Otter Otter runs on Windows PowerShell 5.1, which is already part of Windows 10 and Windows 11. There is nothing extra to install. The otter command runs programs, checks them, starts an interactive session, creates and builds projects, and compiles programs into web applications. What makes it different - Statements read as sentences: age is 29, say "Hello", add 5 to score. - Errors are written for people: the message names the line, says what went wrong in plain words, and suggests a fix. Raw stack traces never reach you. - One small set of ideas covers scripts, desktop apps, web apps, servers, files, data and networking. - No hidden magic: a missing variable is an error, dividing by zero is an error, and text is never silently converted to bytes. Who is Otter for? What can you build? Install Otter

title: Who is Otter for?
text: Who is Otter for? Otter is designed for people who want programs they can read, write and trust - whether or not they have programmed before. People new to programming If you have never written code, Otter lets you concentrate on ideas - values, choices, repetition - instead of punctuation. The first program is one line, and every error message tells you what to try next. Windows users who automate Renaming files, organizing folders, reading CSV, calling a web service, running other programs and capturing their output: these are plain statements in Otter, without learning a shell language first. People building small tools and apps A window with a button, a small web application, an API endpoint, a data viewer. Otter covers desktop and web interfaces with the same readable statements. Teachers and learners Because programs read like sentences, a teacher can read a student program aloud and ask what it means. Otter is small enough to learn end to end. Not for everyone, yet Otter currently runs on Windows only. It is not designed for performance-critical systems programming, and its ecosystem of libraries is young. If you need macOS or Linux support today, Otter is not the right tool yet. What can you build? Install Otter

title: XML

XML XML is a value of its own, not text. You move between the two explicitly: xml from text going in, text from xml coming out. Availability: this feature is in the current source tree and is not part of a published release yet. Building a document catalog is xml with root "library"
library is root of catalog
add element "book" to library and call it book
set attribute "id" of book to "42"
add element "title" with text "Learning Otter" to book

say length of books

each b in books
